name: decrement_strong_count
rules: For Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) to be safe, ptr must have been obtained through Rc::into_raw.
If ptr was obtained through Rc<U>::into_raw and U is sized, U must have the same size and alignment as T for Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) to be safe.
If ptr was obtained through Rc<U>::into_raw and U is unsized, U's data pointer must have the same size and alignment as T for Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) to be safe.
When Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) is invoked, the associated Rc instance must be valid: its strong count must be at least 1.
For Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) to be safe, ptr must point to a block of memory allocated by the global allocator.

Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) may be used to release the final Rc and its backing storage, provided its pointer provenance, layout, allocation, and invocation-time validity requirements are satisfied.
Rc<T>::decrement_strong_count(ptr) must not be called after the final Rc associated with ptr has been released.
